findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous: fields joined with '_' can collide for UIDs containing underscores
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the key by concatenating namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent with '_' separators and no escaping or length prefixing. Resource and folder UIDs in Grafana can contain underscores, so distinct (name, parent) pairs produce identical keys: e.g. name="dash_a", parent="fold_b" and name="dash_a_fold", parent="b" both yield the same key. Because a cached entry means 'deny', a denial recorded for one dashboard/folder combination will incorrectly deny access to a different, unrelated dashboard for up to 30 seconds (shortCacheTTL). Use a delimiter that cannot appear in UIDs, hash the individual fields, or encode lengths to make the key unambiguous.

findings.title: Denial cache is checked before the new DB requery path, reintroducing stale denials for newly granted permissions
findings.body: The stated goal of this PR is to let creators access dashboards/folders they just created by requerying the DB when cached permissions don't contain the resource. However, the denial cache is consulted first in Check and short-circuits before both the permission cache and the DB fallback. If a Check is evaluated and denied before the permission grant is visible (e.g. a check that races the permission write at creation time, or read-replica lag on the permission query), the denial is cached for shortCacheTTL (30s) and every subsequent check for that exact resource returns Allowed=false without ever hitting the DB requery logic added in this PR. The creator is then locked out of the resource they just created for up to 30 seconds — the same symptom this PR is meant to fix. Consider a much shorter TTL for denial entries, or falling through to the DB on denial-cache hit under a singleflight/throttle instead of returning immediately.

findings.title: Denial-cache hits are counted as permission-cache hits in metrics
findings.body: When the denial cache short-circuits a Check, the code increments s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage with label "true" (cache hit). This metric is meant to track usage of the permission cache (permCache); denial-cache hits are a different signal and will inflate the apparent permission cache hit ratio, making dashboards/alerts built on this metric misleading. Consider a separate metric or an additional label value (e.g. "denial") for this path.
